lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Identify the code URL as a portfolio or GitHub profile.
items.because: A generic-looking URL gives recruiters little reason to click it.

items.says: Make sure the linked repositories are polished and relevant.
Confirm that “Ph.D. candidate” reflects formal advancement to candidacy.
items.because: Otherwise, the line should use the institution’s accurate status.

items.says: Add the dissertation or research area.
items.because: The line does not show a doctoral specialization beyond the broad degree name.

items.says: Add an advisor, fellowship, or major academic distinction if relevant.
Add GPA only if it is strong and meaningful.
Consider adding honors or GPA if strong.
Reduce repeated institution and location information if space is tight.
items.because: Both degrees are from the same university.

items.says: Check whether the start date supports marking this role “Present.”
items.because: If the résumé is used before September 2025, it cannot be marked “Present.”

items.says: Keep the bakery role brief.
items.because: It should not occupy space needed for research, publications, or technical work.

items.says: Consider placing the bakery role after directly relevant experience.
items.because: This is a quant-focused résumé.

items.says: Add a measurable budget outcome if one can be substantiated.
items.because: Merely staying within budget is less distinctive than showing the degree of control or improvement.

items.says: Use “labor” instead of “labour” if using U.S. English.
items.because: The location and other conventions suggest U.S. English.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period for the 12% and 7% figures.
items.because: The figures could have been seasonal or based on a short window.

items.says: Make sure “unsold bread” was consistently defined and measured.
Add the asset class or desk context at the role level if permitted.
items.because: Readers currently have to infer it from individual bullets.

items.says: Confirm that the work and metrics can be disclosed.
items.because: Confidentiality obligations may restrict them.

items.says: Specify what “risk-adjusted returns” means.
items.because: It is too vague for a quantitative audience.

items.says: Clarify the baseline for the 35% improvement.
State whether the result was out of sample and after estimated transaction costs.
Distinguish this result from the later Sharpe increase, or consolidate them if they are the same work.
items.because: The two performance claims may look like duplicate descriptions.

items.says: Avoid implying causation beyond what the backtest supports.
Verify that “every backtest decision” also covers preprocessing, features, universe selection, tuning, and model selection.
items.because: Train/test splitting alone does not establish that every decision used only available information.

items.says: Add the number of folds or test windows if it strengthens credibility.
Keep the embargo reference only if a leakage mechanism required it.
items.because: Label overlap or a similar mechanism should justify the embargo.

items.says: Reduce jargon for mixed technical and nontechnical audiences.
Confirm that “feature store” is the correct category.
items.because: A research library, table, or pipeline is not necessarily a governed production feature store.

items.says: Clarify your ownership if others helped design or productionize it.
Quantify scale or efficiency impact if possible.
items.because: Feature count alone may not show the impact.

items.says: Ensure the point-in-time joins were validated against revisions, timestamps, and late-arriving data.
Give the actual outcome if the allocation subsequently went live.
items.because: The bullet currently stops at approval.

items.says: Ensure “approved” does not overstate a preliminary decision if it did not go live.
Clarify what “failure cases” means if space permits.
items.because: They could be stress tests, regime limitations, or operational constraints.

items.says: Avoid confidential allocation details.
Treating the best Sharpe from 400 backtests as expected live Sharpe is invalid.
items.because: Selecting the maximum creates multiple-testing bias and backtest overfitting.

items.says: Explain if this bullet is intended to describe a lesson learned.
items.because: Without that context, recruiters will read it as poor research judgment.

items.says: The order-book imbalance result is repeated under the Kaggle project.
items.because: The repetition makes ownership, provenance, and confidentiality unclear.

items.says: Clarify whether the Sharpe comparison concerns an existing book, a standalone signal, or a combined portfolio.
Add complementary evidence for the Sharpe claim if available.
items.because: Eighteen months is a short evaluation period.

items.says: Confirm that the desk’s Sharpe and performance change may be disclosed.
Distinguish this from the first Northpeak result, or keep only one if they describe the same work.
items.because: The performance claims may be duplicate descriptions.

items.says: Confirm that the title and affiliation reflect your employment status at the time.
items.because: This role predates the stated Ph.D. start.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker can invalidate the Monte Carlo study.
items.because: Workers may generate identical streams, reducing the effective number of independent runs.

items.says: Verify that the claimed log-factor improvement is precise and supported by the manuscript.
Make “my proof” consistent with the paper’s contribution record.

items.says: Avoid implying JASA endorsement.
items.because: The manuscript is only under review there.
